title: EtaleRingInverseImageUnit
statement: Let $U,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $f:U\to V$. Let $b:V_{\mathrm{Et}}\to U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be base change on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Write $L=\mathrm{Scheme.etaleSetPullback}(f)$ for the inverse image of set sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $R$ for sectionwise set direct image, and $R_r$ for sectionwise commutative-ring direct image. Let $F_U,F_V$ forget ring coefficients, and $a:L\dashv R$ be the recorded set adjunction with unit $\eta^a$ and counit $\varepsilon^a$. Assume that $L$ preserves finite limits. There exist a functor $L_r:\mathrm{Sh}(V_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathrm{CommRing})\to\mathrm{Sh}(U_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathrm{CommRing})$, an isomorphism $e:L_r F_U\cong F_V L$, and a natural transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to L_r R_r$ such that, for every ring sheaf $G$, $F_V(\eta_G)=\eta^a_{F_VG}\mathbin{\gg}R(e_G^{-1})$. No adjunction, counit, triangle identity, or hom-set bijection for $L_r$ is asserted. Functor products in these formulas are in diagrammatic order, as in the Lean statement.

source.place: Proposition 00YV, proof of (2), ring paragraph; Section 00YR, sextuples

proof.text: Continuity supplies the set adjunction. Finite-limit preservation gives finite-product preservation; its right adjoint also preserves products.

Choose the ring-sheaf/internal-ring inverse functors on both sites and the lifted ring-object adjunction. Compose the left lifted functor with these inverse functors; the strict underlying identities compose to e.

For the right lifted functor, the product comparison at each base-changed object has the original coordinate projections. Its inverse therefore pairs those coordinates, and the terminal comparison is the unique map of singleton sections. Substitute these descriptions into the five right operation equations of the lifted ring adjunction. The sheaf/internal-object section formulas identify the resulting maps with addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one in the original ring sheaf at that base-changed object. Thus the underlying right comparison and its inverse are sectionwise ring homomorphisms. Naturality of the comparisons gives an isomorphism from the transported right functor to Rr. Transport the lifted unit through it and through the inverse-functor identities. The lifted-unit equation, with the right comparison cancelled, is precisely the stated formula.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleRingInverseImageUnit (U V : Scheme.{u}) (f : U ⟶ V)
    (hL : PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.etaleSetPullback f)) :
    let b := MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ f
    let L := Scheme.etaleSetPullback f
    let R := b.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
      (V.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale) (U.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
    let Rr := b.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u + 1}
      (V.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale) (U.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
    let FrU := sheafForget (D := CommRingCat.{u + 1}) U.smallEtaleTopology
    let FrV := sheafForget (D := CommRingCat.{u + 1}) V.smallEtaleTopology
    let a := Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous b
      (Type (u + 1)) (V.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
      (U.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
    ∃ (Lr : Sheaf V.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1} ⥤
          Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1})
      (er : Lr ⋙ FrU ≅ FrV ⋙ L) (η : 𝟭 _ ⟶ Lr ⋙ Rr),
      ∀ G, FrV.map (η.app G) = a.unit.app (FrV.obj G) ≫ R.map (er.inv.app G)
